item.title: "Bat" "Ilbe Culture"... Ruling Party's Supreme Council Candidates in a Slugfest (“박쥐” “일베 문화”... 與 최고위원 후보들 난타전)
item.description:
"Bat" "Ilbe Culture"... Ruling Party's Supreme Council Candidates in a Slugfest (“박쥐” “일베 문화”... 與 최고위원 후보들 난타전)

Supreme council member candidates of the Democratic Party of Korea engaged in a fierce war of nerves at a broadcast debate on the 3rd, trading remarks such as "self-serving politics," "Ilbe culture," and "bat." (더불어민주당 최고위원 후보들이 3일 방송토론회에서 ‘자기정치’ ‘일베 문화’ ‘박쥐’ 등의 표현을 주고받으며 거친 신경전을 벌였다.)

At the broadcast debate for supreme council member candidates held at OBS Studio in Bucheon, Gyeonggi Province that day, pro-Chung Sae-kyun candidate Han Min-soo said, "One candidate for party leadership made remarks that are utterly unacceptable, claiming the party-government cooperation was thrown into confusion. I wish they would provide evidence of what they have done in terms of self-serving politics" and added, "Attacking for the sake of attacking is not desirable." (이날 경기 부천 OBS 스튜디오에서 열린 최고위원 후보자 방송토론회에서 친청계 한민수 후보는 “어떤 당권주자는 당정 협력을 혼선에 빠뜨렸다는 도저히 수긍할 수 없는 말씀을 하는데 무엇을 하나라도 자기 정치를 했는지 근거를 댔으면 좋겠다”며 “공격하기 위해 하는 건 바람직하지 않다”고 말했다.)

Candidate Choi Min-hee, targeting party leadership candidate Kim Min-seok, said, "When you were prime minister, saying 'being party leader is a dream'—isn't that itself self-serving politics?" Another candidate joined in, saying, "I've never seen a sitting prime minister travel the country for the purpose of public relations," and "I question whether the expression that the party leadership position was his dream was appropriate." (최민희 후보는 김민석 당대표 후보를 겨냥해 “총리 시절 ‘당대표가 로망’이라고 한 것이 오히려 자기 정치 아니냐”고 했고, 한 후보도 “현직 총리가 국정홍보라는 목적으로 전국을 돌아다닌 걸 본 적이 없다”며 “당대표가 본인의 로망이라는 표현이 적합했는지 의문”이라고 가세했다.)

Pro-Lee Jae-myung and pro-Chung Sae-kyun factions also clashed head-on over "Ilbe culture." Pro-Lee candidate Kim Yong demanded, "At the joint rally, Rep. Choi Min-hee labeled the voices of party members as Ilbe culture. Please respond to that." (친명계와 친청계는 ‘일베 문화’를 둘러싸고도 정면 충돌했다. 친명계 김용 후보는 “합동연설회에서 최민희 의원이 당원 목소리를 일베 문화로 규정했는데 답변해 달라”고 따졌다.)

Candidate Choi fired back, "Those claiming to be 'New Lee Jae-myung' held a National Assembly forum mocking President Moon Jae-in and President Roh Moo-hyun and their legacy, and there was all kinds of profanity and ridicule behind the national convention stage. I called that Ilbe culture. If that's not Ilbe culture, what is it?" (최 후보는 “소위 뉴이재명을 주장하는 분들이 국회 토론회를 열어 문재인·노무현 대통령과 그 계승을 조롱한 것, 전당대회장 뒤에서 온갖 욕설과 조롱이 있었던 것을 일베 문화라고 한 것”이라며 “그게 일베 문화가 아니면 무엇이냐”고 맞받았다.)

Candidate Kim Young-ho criticized, "While I was campaigning, Rep. Choi Min-hee called me a 'bat.' This is exactly Ilbe culture, and I find it deeply offensive and humiliating." (김영호 후보는 “제가 유세하는 동안 최민희 의원이 저를 ‘박쥐’라고 했다”며 “이게 바로 일베 문화로 너무나 불쾌하고 모멸감을 느낀다”고 비판했다.)

In response, Candidate Choi said, "I didn't publicly mock him. It was a very quiet remark along the lines of 'what if things turn out this way,' and it ended up on video. If it was conveyed to him, I apologize." (이에 최 후보는 “제가 공개적으로 조롱한 게 아니라 정말 작은 소리로 ‘혹시 이렇게 되지 않을까’라고 한 말이 영상에 들어갔다”며 “본인에게 전달됐다면 사과드린다”고 말했다.)

Then Candidate Kim Yong criticized, "Even if it wasn't made public, isn't it normal to simply not use such expressions going forward? Whether thought or spoken, whether heard or not, such expressions show that Ilbe culture has taken root in you." (그러자 김용 후보는 “공개되지 않았더라도 앞으로 그런 표현 자체를 하지 않는 게 정상 아닌가”라며 “생각이든 말이든, 듣든 못 들었든 그런 표현은 일베 문화가 몸에 밴 것”이라고 비판했다.)

Earlier, on the 1st, when booing was directed at candidate Chung Cheong-rae during the joint rally of the Chungcheong regional primary, Candidate Choi sparked controversy by saying, "Ilbe culture has infiltrated even the joint rally of party leadership," and "I will smash the Ilbe culture that has infiltrated the party." (앞서 최 후보는 지난 1일 충청권 순회경선 합동연설회에서 정청래 후보를 향한 야유가 나오자 “당 지도부 합동연설회에까지 일베 문화가 침투했다”며 “당에 침투한 일베 문화를 박살 내겠다”고 말해 논란이 됐다.)

A spat also erupted over pro-Chung candidate Lee Sung-yoon raising suspicions about candidate Kim Min-seok's absence from the vote on lifting martial law. Candidate Im Mi-ae asked, "The facts have been revealed through the CCTV footage. Do you intend to publicly apologize?" Candidate Lee maintained his existing position. (친청계 이성윤 후보가 김민석 후보의 계엄 해제 표결 불참 의혹을 거론한 것을 두고도 공방이 벌어졌다. 임미애 후보는 “CCTV 공개로 사실관계가 드러났는데 공개 사과할 의향이 있느냐”고 물었고, 이 후보는 기존 입장을 유지했다.)

When asked about the cause of declining support among young voters, Candidate Park Sun-won said, "After the controversy last year over a lawmaker's child's wedding congratulatory money, young people began to leave" and added, "We must reflect on our greed." In response, Candidate Choi rebutted, "I accept the criticism painfully, but I never sent invitations to anyone at any affiliated organization." (박선원 후보는 청년층 지지율 하락 원인을 묻는 질문에서 “지난해 한 의원 자녀 결혼식 축의금 논란 이후 청년들이 떠나기 시작했다”며 “탐욕스러운 모습을 반성해야 한다”고 말했다. 이에 최 후보는 “지적은 아프게 받아들이지만 산하기관 누구에게도 청첩장을 보낸 적은 없다”고 반박했다.)

Additionally, Candidate Kim Yong, regarding Candidate Han's claim that he "stopped the bleeding with his handkerchief" when President Lee was attacked in Gadeokdo, said, "I cannot forgive someone who was at the scene and claims to be pro-Lee but makes false statements," and "I ask the three members of 'Team Chung Cheong-rae' to engage in politics that resonates with the public." Kim also said that if it is untrue, a public apology should be made. (또 김용 후보는 한 후보가 이 대통령 가덕도 피습 당시 ‘제 손수건으로 지혈을 했다’고 한 것과 관련해 “현장에 있던 사람이 친명을 자처하면서 잘못 말하는 것을 용서할 수 없다”며 “‘팀정청래’ 세 분은 국민에게 공감되는 정치활동을 해달라”고 했다. 김 후보는 사실과 다르다면 공개 사과해야 한다고도 했다.)

item.title: "Hell Has Opened" Busan Kick Attack Victim to Discuss Supplementary Investigation Powers with Han Dong-hoon (“지옥 열렸다” 돌려차기 피해자, 한동훈과 보완수사권 대담)
item.description:
"Hell Has Opened" Busan Kick Attack Victim to Discuss Supplementary Investigation Powers with Han Dong-hoon (“지옥 열렸다” 돌려차기 피해자, 한동훈과 보완수사권 대담)

Kim Jin-joo (pseudonym), the victim of the "Busan kick attack case," will attend a roundtable hosted by independent lawmaker Han Dong-hoon's office. One day before the roundtable, on the 3rd, Kim posted a comment on the social media (SNS) of Kim Yong-min, a Democratic Party lawmaker who proposed a revision to the Criminal Procedure Act abolishing prosecutors' direct investigative powers, saying, "Go to hell." (‘부산 돌려차기 사건’의 피해자 김진주(가명)씨가 무소속 한동훈 의원실이 주최한 간담회에 참석한다. 간담회를 하루 앞둔 3일 김씨는 검찰의 직접 수사권을 폐지하는 형사소송법 개정안을 발의한 김용민 더불어민주당 의원의 소셜미디어(SNS)에 “지옥에나 가세요”라는 댓글을 달았다.)

Han is set to hold a roundtable titled "Ban on Supplementary Investigation, Hell's Gate Has Opened" at the National Assembly Members' Office Building on the afternoon of the 4th. At this event, Kim, the victim of the Busan kick attack case—where prosecutors uncovered evidence of sexual violence through supplementary investigation that police had ignored—will hold a conversation with Han. Additionally, footage of Kim being questioned by police during the Busan kick attack case will be released. Kim is also expected to take questions from reporters alongside Han after the roundtable. (한 의원은 오는 4일 오후 국회 의원회관에서 ‘보완 수사 금지, 지옥문이 열렸다’ 간담회를 열 예정이다. 이 자리에서는 경찰이 무시한 성범죄 증거를 검찰이 보완 수사해 찾아낸 ‘부산 돌려차기 사건’의 피해자 김씨가 한 의원과 대담한다. 이와 함께 부산 돌려차기 사건 당시 김씨가 경찰에서 조사받는 화면도 공개할 예정이다. 김씨는 간담회 이후 한 의원과 함께 취재진 질의에도 응할 것으로 알려졌다.)

Separately, Han's side sent a notice to all 299 lawmakers from both ruling and opposition parties, stating, "Any lawmaker who attends the roundtable is free to speak as they wish" and "If you reply in advance about your attendance, we will guarantee ample opportunity to speak." Earlier, on the 29th of last month, Han had also requested all 161 Democratic Party lawmakers to "debate in a proper public forum," but none of the Democratic lawmakers who supported abolishing supplementary investigation powers attended. (이와 별개로 한 의원 측은 여야 국회의원 299명 전원(全員)에게 “간담회에 참석하시는 의원님 누구든 자유롭게 발언하실 수 있다”며 “의원님 참석 여부를 미리 회신해 주신다면 충분한 발언 기회도 보장하겠다”는 취지의 알림도 발송했다. 한 의원은 이보다 앞서 지난달 29일에도 민주당 소속 의원 161명 모두에게 “제대로 된 공론장에서 토론하자”고 요청했지만, 보완 수사권 폐지에 찬성한 민주당 의원들은 아무도 참석하지 않았다.)

Kim, the victim of the Busan kick attack case, said in a media interview on the 31st of last month, after the National Assembly passed the bill to abolish supplementary investigation powers (the Criminal Procedure Act revision) proposed by Democratic lawmaker Kim Yong-min, that "(In my case) supplementary investigation was the 'last cliff' for approaching the truth" and that "It gives the opportunity to correct here (at the prosecution) what wasn't caught here (at the police investigation stage), but abolishing it eliminates that opportunity." (부산 돌려차기 사건의 피해자 김씨는 지난달 31일 민주당 김용민 의원이 발의한 보완 수사권 폐지법(형소법 개정안)이 국회 본회의를 통과하자 언론 인터뷰에서 “(제 사건에서) 보완 수사권은 진실에 다가가는 ‘최후의 절벽’이었다”며 “보완 수사권이 여기(경찰 수사 단계)에서 잡지 못했더라도 여기(검찰)서는 바로잡을 수 있다는 기회를 주는 것인데, 폐지는 이 기회를 없애버리는 것”이라고 했다.)

After the bill passed, Kim Yong-min posted a photo taken at former President Roh Moo-hyun's grave on SNS, writing, "Thinking of the painful sacrifice (Roh) had to endure alone before the blade of absolute power—especially the political prosecution—my heart always feels heavy." Along with this, Kim also posted a video of himself offering an envelope containing the Criminal Procedure Act revision at Roh's grave. In response, Kim Jin-joo wrote on his post: "Go to hell —Kim Jin-joo, Busan kick attack victim—." The comment was later hidden by Instagram. (법안이 통과된 이후 김 의원은 노무현 전 대통령 묘역에서 촬영한 사진을 SNS에 올리면서 “(노 전 대통령이) 무소불위의 권력, 특히 정치 검찰의 칼날 앞에 홀로 감내하셔야 했던 그 아픈 희생을 생각하면 늘 가슴이 먹먹해진다”고 했다. 이와 함께 김 의원은 자신이 노 전 대통령 묘역에 형소법 개정안이 담긴 봉투를 바치는 장면을 SNS에 올리기도 했다. 그러자 김씨는 김 의원의 해당 게시물에 “지옥에나 가세요 –부산돌려차기피해자 김진주-”라고 적었다. 이후 김씨 댓글은 인스타그램 측에 의해 숨김 처리됐다.)

In 2022, Kim was struck on the back of the head by a man she had never met and nearly lost her life. The suspect stomped on the fallen Kim to render her unconscious, dragged her to a blind spot in surveillance cameras, and attempted sexual assault. At the police investigation stage, the case was only referred to prosecutors on charges of attempted murder, but the attempted sexual assault was uncovered through supplementary investigation by the prosecution at the appeals court stage. <<>> (2022년 김씨는 일면식도 없던 남성에게 뒷머리를 돌려차기로 가격당하고 목숨을 잃을 뻔했다. 피의자는 쓰러진 김씨를 발로 밟아서 의식을 잃게 하고, 감시 카메라의 사각지대로 끌고 가 성폭행을 시도했다. 당시 경찰 수사 단계에선 살인 미수 혐의로만 송치됐으나, 항소심 단계에서 검찰의 보완 수사를 통해 성폭행 시도가 밝혀졌다.)

item.title: Military Removes 1st Corps Commander from Duty Over 'Empty Rifle' Guard Directive (軍, ‘빈총 경계’ 지침 내린 1군단장 직무 배제)
item.description:
Military Removes 1st Corps Commander from Duty Over 'Empty Rifle' Guard Directive (軍, ‘빈총 경계’ 지침 내린 1군단장 직무 배제)

The Ministry of National Defense announced on the 3rd that it has removed Lieutenant General Han Ki-sung, commander of the Army's 1st Corps, from duty after he changed guard duty guidelines to prohibit loading live ammunition into crew-served weapons deployed at front-line guard posts (GPs) and general outposts (GOPs), sparking controversy over "lax combat readiness." The ministry said, "In connection with the inspection and investigation into recent matters related to the 1st Corps, the current corps commander has been removed from duty as of today," adding, "During this period, the Army Education and Training Command commander will serve as acting 1st Corps commander." <<> There was also an incident at the Army's 1st Corps on the 30th of last month in which a subordinate unit mistook a U.S. military reconnaissance drone—launched as part of a ROK-U.S. combined exercise—for an "unidentified aerial vehicle" and nearly attempted to intercept it. It was revealed that the incident occurred because a 1st Corps staff member, despite having received advance notice of the drone flight plan from the U.S. military, failed to report it to higher command. There is analysis that the military has thus acknowledged command responsibility for this series of problems. <<> Corps commander Han, a product of the ROTC program, was appointed in November of last year as commander of the 1st Corps—responsible for front-line defense of the western front and the defense of Seoul—becoming the first non-Korea Military Academy graduate to hold the post. However, it was revealed that starting in the first half of this year, the 1st Corps had not loaded live ammunition into its key crew-served weapons, the K6 heavy machine gun and the K4 high-velocity grenade machine gun, during guard duty, and that a directive change by Corps Commander Han was behind this [see this newspaper's July 29 issue, page A1, etc.], sparking controversy. <<> ◇Emergency Commanders' Meeting Called by An Kyu-baek: "Conduct a Comprehensive Inspection of Combat Discipline Across All Forces" <<> Minister of National Defense An Kyu-baek held an emergency meeting of major commanders from all forces on the afternoon of the 3rd at the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) operations command center in Yongsan, Seoul, and ordered the formation of a "Joint Special Discipline Inspection Task Force" led by the Ministry of National Defense Inspector General to "conduct a focused inspection of combat discipline and reporting systems across all forces, including the 1st Corps, before the conclusion of the UFS (Ulchi Freedom Shield) exercise." Minister An reportedly stated, "The core of unit operations lies in current operations based on fundamentals and principles, and in realistic education and training," adding, "Through this, we must stand tall as a strong military that the people trust, that enemies fear, and that does not collapse in the face of any threat." <<> The Ministry of National Defense stated that the meeting was held "to comprehensively review combat readiness in light of the recent shortcomings in operational discipline," and that JCS Chairman Kim Myung-soo, the chiefs of staff of each service, operations commanders, and commanders of ministry direct-report units and joint units attended. Participants reportedly discussed strengthening on-site command activities and improving response capabilities through realistic training to establish operational discipline and combat readiness. <<> Earlier, the Army Ground Operations Command (GOC) began inspections of guard operations at subordinate front-line corps, including the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 5th Corps and the Capital Corps, which includes the 2nd Marine Division, starting on the 30th of last month. The large-scale inspection came after it became known that the 1st Corps—a key corps tasked with defending the Imjin River estuary and the northern outskirts of Seoul while facing North Korean forces—had not loaded live ammunition into its K6 heavy machine guns and K4 high-velocity grenade machine guns during guard duty since the first half of this year. <<> However, on the very day the GOC began its inspection of guard operations, the 1st Corps again issued a "Crane" alert and initiated air defense operations after determining that a U.S. military reconnaissance drone—detected by thermal observation devices (TOD) and local air defense radar—was an "unidentified aerial vehicle." As a result, the JCS Combat Readiness Inspection Office visited the 1st Corps on the 31st of last month to investigate. <<> The military leadership took this situation seriously, leading to the decision to remove Lieutenant General Han Ki-sung from duty. However, no specific charges have been confirmed against Corps Commander Han; military authorities will reportedly continue their investigation following the temporary removal from duty. <<> In announcing the results of its investigation into the drone incident on the 3rd, the JCS stated, "The reporting system along the chain of command did not function properly." In other words, it occurred because a Korean staff member failed to properly report to higher command. Furthermore, it was reported that there were also shortcomings in the airspace control procedures between the ROK and U.S. militaries. While regulations require prior approval from the Army GOC or the Air Force Operations Command (AFOC) depending on the altitude at which a drone would fly, in practice, this procedure was not always followed, and there was a habit of simply completing coordination through informal contact between working-level officials. <<> According to the JCS, a U.S. military official notified a 1st Corps staff member via text message of the flight plan the day before the drone flight—which was part of the annual ROK-U.S. Marine Corps combined exercise KMEP—on the 29th of last month. The 1st Corps staff member did not report the plan to higher command or disseminate it to relevant units, but simply replied by text message to the U.S. side that "there are no (flight) restrictions." <<> The official document attached by the U.S. military to the text message specified the drone's altitude, but the 1st Corps staff member did not verify it and assumed it was the "low-altitude drone flight" he typically handled. In reality, it was a "high-altitude flight" requiring AFOC approval, but having received a response that there were no restrictions, the U.S. military launched the drone as planned. This led to a situation where a subordinate 1st Corps unit mistook it for an "unidentified aerial vehicle" and prepared to intercept it. This would not have occurred if either side's working-level personnel had taken steps to verify the drone's flight altitude and followed the prescribed approval procedures. <<> A JCS official said, "This case confirms the need to adhere to the ROK-U.S. airspace control procedures as prescribed," adding, "Going forward, we will improve the airspace control coordination system based on close communication between the ROK and the U.S." (국방부가 최전방 감시초소(GP)와 일반전초(GOP)에 배치된 공용화기에 실탄을 삽탄(揷彈)하지 않도록 경계 근무 지침을 변경해 ‘경계 태세 소홀’ 논란을 일으킨 한기성 육군 1군단장(중장)을 직무 배제 조치했다고 3일 밝혔다. 국방부는 이날 “최근 1군단 관련 사안에 대한 점검 및 조사와 관련해 현 군단장을 오늘부로 직무배제했다”며 “해당 기간 동안 육군교육사령관이 1군단장을 직무대리할 예정”이라고 밝혔다.)

item.title: President Lee Holds Over 7-Hour Closed-Door Meeting on 'Real Estate and Stock Market' Immediately Upon Return (李 귀국하자마자 7시간 넘게 ‘부동산·증시’ 비공개 회의)
item.description:
President Lee Holds Over 7-Hour Closed-Door Meeting on 'Real Estate and Stock Market' Immediately Upon Return (李 귀국하자마자 7시간 넘게 ‘부동산·증시’ 비공개 회의)

President Lee Jae-myung, who returned home on the morning of the 3rd after completing an 11-day tour of the United States and South America, took a helicopter from the airport straight to the presidential office, where he presided over a closed-door meeting from 3 p.m. to 10:30 p.m.—a total of 7 hours and 30 minutes—to review domestic issues such as real estate policy and the stock market. (11일간의 미국·남미 순방 일정을 마치고 3일 오전 귀국한 이재명 대통령은 공항에서 헬기를 타고 곧바로 청와대로 이동해 오후 3시부터 밤 10시 30분까지 7시간 30분간 부동산 정책과 주식시장 등 국내 현안을 점검하는 비공개 회의를 주재했다.)

At the meeting, President Lee said, "The sluggish housing supply that has persisted since 2022 has created a supply cliff situation," and "To overcome this, supply and its speed are very important." He then added, "Secure as much available supply as possible so that a large number of homes can be provided quickly." (이 자리에서 이 대통령은 “2022년부터 지속된 주택 공급 부진이 공급 절벽 상황을 초래했다”며 “이를 극복하기 위해서는 공급과 그 속도가 매우 중요하다”고 했다. 이어 “신속하게 많은 주택이 공급될 수 있게 가용한 공급 물량을 최대한 확보하라”고도 했다.)

Dinner was handled with boxed meals in the middle of the meeting. In addition to the presidential staff, the cabinet, including Prime Minister Han Sung-sook and Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs Koo Yoon-cheol, also attended. The meeting has been interpreted as an expression of a sense of crisis over opposition to policies on real estate, stocks, and the decline in the president's approval rating. (저녁 식사도 회의 중간에 도시락으로 해결했다. 회의에는 청와대 참모진 외에 한성숙 국무총리와 구윤철 경제부총리 등 내각도 참석했다. 부동산, 주식 등 정책에 대한 반대 여론과 대통령 지지율 하락 등의 상황에 대한 위기감의 발로라는 해석이 나왔다.)

At the meeting, the '2026 Tax Reform Plan' announced by the Ministry of Economy and Finance was discussed, and it is said that the mood of voters in the capital region—sensitive to real estate issues—was also on the agenda. The core of the reform plan includes differentiated taxation for owner-occupied versus non-owner-occupied homes and raising the comprehensive real estate tax rate on high-priced homes valued at around 4 billion won. The opposition criticized it, saying, "The first thing he threw out upon returning was a tax bomb." President Lee is said to have reviewed the impact this tax reform plan would have on public sentiment. (이날 회의에서는 재정경제부가 발표한 ‘2026년 세제 개편안’이 논의됐는데, 부동산에 민감한 수도권 민심 향방도 논의됐다고 한다. 실거주·비거주 주택 차등 과세, 시가 40억원대의 고가 주택에 대한 종합부동산세 세율 인상 등이 이번 개편안의 골자다. 야권에서는 “귀국하자마자 던진 것이 세금 폭탄”이라는 비판이 나왔다. 이 대통령은 이번 세제 개편안이 민심에 미칠 영향 등을 점검한 것으로 전해졌다.)

Regarding the stock market, reports were given on the recent sharp drop in the KOSPI and the fallout from single-stock leveraged ETFs. (주식시장과 관련해서는 최근 코스피 급락과 단일 종목 레버리지 ETF 파장 등에 대한 보고가 이뤄졌다고 한다.)

Behind President Lee's decision to hold a closed-door meeting immediately after returning is believed to be a sense of crisis stemming from the recent decline in approval ratings for his administration. In particular, since the main driver of the falling approval ratings is instability in the real estate and stock markets, he appears to have hastened related discussions. However, no measures that could immediately impact the markets emerged that day. A presidential office official said, "It's difficult to come up with special measures right away," and added, "There are also signs that it could devolve into a blame game over responsibility." (이 대통령이 귀국 직후 비공개 회의를 연 배경에는 최근 국정 지지율 하락에 따른 위기감이 깔린 것으로 풀이된다. 특히 지지율 하락의 주요인이 부동산·주식 시장 불안이기 때문에 관련 논의를 서두른 것으로 보인다. 그러나 이날 당장 시장에 영향을 줄 수 있는 대책은 나오지 않았다. 청와대 관계자는 “당장 특단의 대책을 마련하긴 어려운 상황”이라며 “책임 소재 공방으로 흐르는 조짐도 있다”고 전했다.)

The real estate and stock issues have dragged down President Lee's approval ratings. According to a survey conducted by pollster Realmeter from the 27th to 31st of last month, 45.9% of respondents positively evaluated President Lee's performance, the lowest since he took office. Negative evaluations stood at 50.5%. Realmeter said, "Economic instability caused by the stock market crash and the leveraged ETF fallout, controversies over real estate taxation and the constitutional amendment for presidential term extension, and the forced passage of legislation abolishing the prosecution's supplementary investigative powers all acted in combination." (부동산과 주식 문제는 이 대통령의 지지율을 끌어내렸다. 여론조사 업체 리얼미터가 지난달 27~31일 조사한 결과에 따르면, 이 대통령의 국정 수행을 긍정적으로 평가한 응답자는 45.9%로, 취임 후 최저치를 기록했다. 부정 평가는 50.5%였다. 리얼미터는 “증시 폭락과 레버리지 상장지수펀드(ETF) 파장에 따른 경제적 불안정성, 부동산 세제 및 대통령 연임 개헌 논란, 검찰 보완 수사권 폐지 입법 강행 등이 복합적으로 작용했다”고 했다.)

Internally, the presidential office has also seen a rise in blame over this. The target is Kim Yong-beom, the presidential office's policy chief. On the 28th (local time), at a press briefing in Brazil, Kim cited 'the dynamism of individual investors' as a primary cause of the extreme volatility in the stock market, and it is said that the presidential staff remaining in South Korea were greatly taken aback. Another presidential office official said, "It doesn't look good at all for the architect of the system to blame investors." This has been contrasted with the financial authorities' chiefs, who canceled their scheduled vacations and bowed their heads, saying 'we are sorry,' when the stock market crashed last week. (청와대 내부에서는 이를 두고 책임론도 불거졌다. 대상은 김용범 청와대 정책실장이다. 김 실장은 28일(현지 시각) 브라질 현지 기자 브리핑에서 주식 시장의 극심한 변동성의 원인으로 ‘개인 투자자의 역동성’ 등을 주된 원인으로 지목했고, 국내에 남아 있던 청와대 참모들은 크게 당황했다고 한다. 다른 청와대 관계자는 “제도 설계자가 투자자를 탓하는 모양새가 매우 좋지 않다”고 했다. 지난주 증시가 폭락할 때 금융 당국 수장들이 예정된 휴가를 취소하고 ‘송구하다’며 고개를 숙인 것과는 대조적이라는 평가가 나왔다.)

The instability in asset markets is also putting pressure on the ruling party. The ruling party maintains that there were no party-government consultations at the time the leveraged ETFs were introduced. Among ruling party lawmakers, complaints are emerging that while party-government consultations were closely held at all levels during the Moon Jae-in administration, the density of such consultations has declined under the Lee Jae-myung administration. A presidential office official said, "There are a mountain of issues the president needs to coordinate." (자산 시장 불안은 여당에도 부담을 주고 있다. 여당은 레버리지 ETF 도입 당시 당정 협의가 없었다는 입장이다. 여당 의원들 사이에서는 문재인 정부 때는 당정 협의가 각급에서 긴밀하게 이뤄졌지만, 이재명 정부 들어서는 당정 협의의 밀도가 떨어졌다는 불만이 나오고 있다. 청와대 관계자는 “대통령이 조율해야 할 문제가 산적해 있다”고 했다.)

item.title: [Chapter 34] No Need to Get Angry at a Barking Dog ([34화] 짖는 개에게 화낼 필요는 없다)
item.description:
[Chapter 34] No Need to Get Angry at a Barking Dog ([34화] 짖는 개에게 화낼 필요는 없다)

☞ Start from Chapter 1 (☞ 1화부터 보기)

☞ Character Introductions (☞ 등장인물 소개)

Irina tightened her grip on Evan's hand as she retraced old memories. Outside the hospital window, Tokyo's nightscape blurred into haze. (이리나는 옛 기억을 되짚으며 에반의 손을 꽉 잡았다. 병실의 창밖으로 도쿄의 야경이 흐릿하게 번졌다.)

The stiff-backed man who once stood against three-to-one odds in London now lay asleep, wrapped in bandages, unable even to call Irina's name. (런던에서 3대1 앞에 서던 그 뻣뻣한 남자가, 지금은 붕대에 감긴 채 이리나의 이름도 부르지 못하고 잠들었다.)

The smell of antiseptic in the hospital room stirred Irina's old memories. The winter in Bucharest, the sounds heard through the walls, the wailing of her family, shattering plates, and the silence that came unexpectedly one day. (병실의 소독약 냄새가 이리나의 오래된 기억을 건드렸다. 부쿠레슈티의 겨울, 벽 너머로 들리던 소리들, 가족들의 울부짖음, 깨지는 접시, 그리고 어느 날 갑자기 찾아온 적막.)

The sound of the front door closing was her last memory of her father's retreating figure. (현관문이 닫히는 소리가 아버지의 뒷모습을 본 마지막 기억이었다.)

Twelve-year-old Irina couldn't tell whether that silence meant freedom or abandonment. She filled her mother's empty place by preparing her siblings' breakfasts, and after school she hauled loads at the market. That's when she learned her body had worth. (열두 살의 이리나는 그 적막이 자유를 얻은 것인지, 버려진 것인지 구분하지 못했다. 엄마의 빈자리를 채우듯 동생들의 아침을 차리고, 학교가 끝나면 시장에서 짐을 날랐다. 몸이 쓸모 있다는 걸 안 건 그 무렵이다.)

To protect her own family, she first had to learn how to fight back. That's how fighting became a livelihood, and the livelihood became a career. (제 식구를 지키려면, 맞서는 법을 먼저 배워야 했다. 그렇게 싸움은 생계가 됐고, 생계는 직업이 됐다.)

In Irina's memory, men left either wounds or empty spaces. There were no exceptions. But this man was neither. (이리나의 기억 속 남자들은 상처를 남기거나 빈자리를 남겼다. 예외는 없었다. 그런데 이 남자는 둘 다 아니었다.)

Evan's fingers twitched faintly in his sleep. Irina didn't let go of his hand. (에반의 손가락이 잠결에 미세하게 움직였다. 이리나는 그 손을 놓지 않았다.)

He couldn't even fight, yet he didn't run. Even while taking hits, he shielded Irina behind his back. I've protected others before, but no one has ever protected me. (싸움도 못 하면서 도망가지 않았다. 맞으면서도 이리나를 등 뒤로 감쌌다. 내가 누군가를 지켜준 적은 있지만, 누군가 나를 지켜준 적은 없으니까.)

A few weeks after Evan's accident in Tokyo, Vice President Patrick convened a sales strategy meeting. Even if a piece falls on the chessboard, the game goes on. (에반의 도쿄 사고 후 몇 주 후, 패트릭 부사장은 영업 전략 회의를 소집했다. 체스판의 말이 쓰러져도 게임은 계속되는 법.)

The clock at Dudael Tech raced forward like an arrow, with no time—or more precisely, no inclination—to worry about the wounded. (듀다엘 테크의 시계는 부상자를 신경 쓸 겨를도 없이, 아니 정확히는 신경도 쓰지 않은 채, 화살처럼 앞으로 나아갔다.)

Even before the meeting began, Patrick had put Dudael's sales performance data up on the large screen. This quarter's results were close to the finance team's guidance, but Patrick had no intention whatsoever of congratulating them on hitting their targets. Because the pinnacle of a vast organization isn't earned through performance or performance reviews alone. (패트릭은 회의가 시작하기도 전에 대형 스크린 화면에 듀다엘의 매출 현황 자료를 띄워놓았다. 이번 분기 실적은 재무팀 가이던스에 근접했지만, 패트릭은 목표 달성을 격려할 생각이 추호도 없었다. 거대 조직의 정점은, 실적이나 인사 평가로만 얻는 것이 아니기 때문이다.)

Inside the conference room, with external light blocked out, only the blue glow of the large display swirled. On the screen, the global status of Sariel contract negotiations flickered in red and yellow dots. (회의실 안은 외부의 빛이 차단된 공간에 대형 디스플레이의 청색광만 감돌았다. 화면에는 전 세계 사리엘 계약 추진 현황이 붉은색과 노란색 점으로 깜빡였다.)

When Patrick rose with his neck held straight, the low murmuring in the conference room fell silent. The executives swallowed dryly behind their shirt collars and studied Patrick's expression. (패트릭이 목을 곧게 세운 채로 일어서자, 회의실에서 낮게 웅성대던 소리가 사라졌다. 임원들은 셔츠 깃 뒤로 마른침을 삼키며 패트릭의 안색을 살폈다.)

Instead of taking the head seat, Patrick slowly circled the conference table. (패트릭은 상석에 앉는 대신 회의 테이블 주위를 천천히 돌았다.)

The rhythmic sound of his dress shoes striking the marble was chilling. Patrick's gaze stopped on Jeff Ballinger, who was attending this meeting for the first time. Jeff offered an awkward smile to hide his nerves. (구두 굽이 대리석에 부딪히는 규칙적인 소리가 공포감을 자아냈다. 패트릭의 시선이 이번 회의에 처음 참석한 제프 밸린저에게 멈췄다. 제프는 긴장을 감추려 어색한 미소를 지어 보였다.)

"What's your name?" (“이름이 뭐지?”)

"Jeff Ballinger. I was just transferred from the Korean branch to headquarters. It's an honor to be at this meeting." (“제프 밸린저입니다. 한국 지사에서 본사로 막 발령받았습니다. 이 자리에 참석하게 되어 영광입니다.”)

Patrick didn't return the smile. Instead, he looked Jeff over from shoulder to cuff. With two fingers, he lightly flicked the lapel of Jeff's suit. (패트릭은 미소를 돌려주지 않았다. 대신 제프의 어깨부터 소매 끝까지 훑었다. 두 손가락으로 제프의 수트 라펠을 가볍게 튕겼다.)

"How much did this suit cost?" (“이 옷은 얼마짜린가?”)

"Excuse me? Ah... I purchased it from Brooks Brothers." (“네? 아…… 브룩스 브라더스에서 구매한 것입니다만.")

"Brooks Brothers?" (“브룩스 브라더스?”)

A sneer curled at the corner of Patrick's mouth. The suit didn't matter. The name didn't matter either. The first person who takes a hit without fighting back becomes the sacrificial lamb of the conference room. (패트릭의 입가에 비웃음이 걸렸다. 옷은 상관없었다. 이름도 상관없었다. 맞고도 반격하지 않는 첫 번째 사람이, 회의실의 제물이 된다.)

"You're the man who sells the eyes of God worth hundreds of millions of dollars. And you stand before clients wearing mass-produced off-the-rack suits?" (“자네는 지금 수억 달러짜리 신의 눈을 팔러 다니는 사람이야. 그런데 대량 생산된 기성복을 걸치고 고객 앞에 선다고?”)

"I'll make sure to wear proper attire at meetings from now on." (“앞으로 회의엔 꼭 좋은 옷을 입고 오겠습니다.”)

"It's not in front of me—wearing proper attire in front of clients is the bare minimum!" (“내 앞에서가 아니라 고객들 앞에서 좋은 옷을 입는 건 기본 중의 기본이야!”)

Patrick's shout struck the ceiling. (패트릭의 고함이 천장을 때렸다.)

"Who would trust a system sold by a man who walks around in cheap clothes? You really have no fundamentals!" (“싸구려 옷을 입고 다니는 놈이 파는 시스템을 누가 신뢰하겠나? 정말이지 기본이 안 돼 있군!”)

Jeff bowed his head. The other executives, as if by unspoken agreement, fixed their eyes on the meeting materials. Patrick immediately pointed at the map on the screen. (제프는 고개를 숙였다. 다른 임원들은 약속이라도 한 듯 회의 자료로 시선을 박았다. 패트릭은 곧바로 화면 속 지도를 가리켰다.)

"What about the situation in Japan? Isn't this the point where signing a contract today wouldn't be out of line?" (“일본 상황은 어때? 여기는 오늘 당장 계약을 체결해도 이상하지 않은 시점 아닌가?”)

Jeff cleared his throat and picked up the briefing folder. It was to buy time. The other executives all dropped their heads at once. (제프가 헛기침을 하며 브리핑 폴더를 집어 들었다. 시간을 벌기 위해서였다. 다른 임원들은 일제히 고개를 떨궜다.)

"We're currently in close consultation with the Japanese government. Coordinating through multiple channels..." (“현재 일본 정부와 긴밀히 협의 중이라고 합니다. 여러 채널을 통해 조율을....”)

"In consultation?" Patrick cut Jeff off as if he'd been waiting for that exact word. (“협의 중?” 패트릭이 제프의 말을 기다렸다는 듯 잘랐다.)

"Next time you come, bring a signed contract instead of those words. Or bring your resignation." (“다음에 올 때는 그 말 대신 서명이 찍힌 계약서를 가져와. 아니면 사표를 들고 오든지.”)

Leaving Jeff's frightened face behind, Patrick's cold gaze moved to the person in charge of South America. (제프의 겁먹은 표정을 뒤로한 채 패트릭의 서늘한 시선이 남미 담당자에게 옮겨갔다.)

"What about South America?" (“남미 쪽은?”)

"We're examining from multiple angles whether to enter Peru or Chile first, considering the security conditions." (“페루와 칠레 중 어느 국가에 먼저 진출할지 안보 여건을 다각적으로 검토하고 있습니다.”)

Patrick slammed his fist on Chile's coastline on the map. (패트릭이 지도의 칠레 해안선을 주먹으로 내리쳤다.)

"Look at the length of Chile's border. Only a fool wouldn't know where Sariel's main market is. You're not sitting here to 'review.' Prove it with results, right now." (“칠레의 국경선 길이를 봐. 바보가 아닌 이상 어디가 사리엘의 주 시장인지 모를 수가 있나? 당신들은 여기서 검토나 하라고 앉아 있는 게 아니야. 당장 성과로 증명해.”)

Patrick strode out like a stage actor who'd just delivered his closing lines. No one moved until the sound of his shoes completely faded at the end of the hallway. (패트릭은 마치 대사를 끝낸 연극 배우처럼 자리를 박차고 나갔다. 구두 소리가 복도 끝에서 완전히 사라질 때까지 아무도 움직이지 않았다.)

Once in the private elevator, Patrick checked his appearance in the metal walls. The flush from shouting in the meeting had already returned to calm. (전용 엘리베이터에 올라탄 패트릭은 금속 벽면에 비친 자신의 매무새를 확인했다. 회의실 고함으로 달아올랐던 안색은 이미 평온을 되찾았다.)

He pulled out his smartphone and sent a short message. (주머니에서 스마트폰을 꺼내 짧은 메시지를 보냈다.)

The recipient was Alistair Carrington, the old-money tycoon who held Dudael's capital lifeline. (수신인은 앨리스터 캐링턴, 듀다엘의 자본 줄기를 쥐고 있는 올드 머니 거물.)

"Your plan may be able to move forward a little faster." (“당신의 계획이 조금 더 빨리 추진될 수 있을 겁니다.”)

Patrick's face, pressing the send button, was reflected coldly in the elevator walls. (전송 버튼을 누르는 패트릭의 얼굴이 엘리베이터 벽면에 차갑게 반사됐다.)

To him, a subordinate's humiliation was merely cheap fuel to accelerate business. (그에게 부하 직원의 수치심은 사업 속도를 높이기 위한 값싼 연료에 불과했다.)

Jeff was left alone in the empty conference room. He grabbed his suit sleeve roughly, then loosened his tie. There was only one way to recover the pride Patrick had trampled on: squeezing a weaker link than himself. (텅 빈 대회의실에 제프만 덩그러니 남았다. 수트 소매를 거칠게 움켜쥐었다가, 넥타이를 풀어 헤쳤다. 패트릭이 짓밟고 간 자존심을 회복할 방법은 하나뿐이었다. 자신보다 약한 고리를 쥐어짜는 것.)

Jeff picked up his smartphone and called Evan. It connected after two rings. (제프는 스마트폰을 집어 들어 에반에게 전화를 걸었다. 신호음 두 번 만에 연결됐다.)

"Yes, this is Evan." (“네, 에반입니다.”)

Evan's voice was businesslike. No pain, no fear in it. (에반의 목소리는 사무적이었다. 통증이나 두려움은 느껴지지 않았다.)

"You're not lying in your hospital bed watching Netflix, are you?" (“자네, 지금 병상에 누워서 넷플릭스나 보고 있을 때는 아닐 텐데?”)

Jeff's voice was sharp, mimicking Patrick's. The one who'd just been hit striking the next person—a common food chain in the defense industry. (제프의 목소리는 패트릭의 그것을 흉내 내듯 날카로웠다. 방금 맞은 자가 다음 사람을 때리는, 방산 업계에서 흔한 먹이사슬이었다.)

"Just tell me what you need." (“용건만 말씀하십시오.”)

"What? What I need?" (“뭐? 용건?”)

Jeff's brow twitched. (제프의 눈썹이 꿈틀거렸다.)

"What I need to hear from you isn't your hospital admission report—it's the Philippine Ministry of Defense contract!" (“내 귀에 들어와야 할 건 자네 병원 입원 보고가 아니라, 필리핀 국방부 계약서야!”)

Imagining himself as a tough guy, he kicked the chair awkwardly. (머릿속 터프한 모습을 그리며, 부자연스럽게 의자를 발로 걷어찼다.)

"Vice President Patrick is going crazy demanding results right now, and what are you doing over there? I told you last week to meet the defense ministry people and put pressure on them. Stop with that vague 'in consultation' nonsense and get the contract stamped right now." (“패트릭 부사장님이 지금 당장 성과를 가져오라고 난리인데 거기서 뭐 하고 있는 거야. 지난주에도 방위성 사람 만나서 압박하라고 했잖아. ‘협의 중’이라는 뜬구름 잡는 소리 말고 당장 계약서 도장 받아내.”)

"Understood." (“알겠습니다.”)

"And what about Thailand?" (“그리고 태국은?”)

"We're in the feasibility study stage." (“사업 타당성 검토 단계입니다.”)

"That's what I mean—speed it up! Contact someone for the Philippines, a broker or whoever, and set up a meeting immediately. Get everything ready so you can fly to Manila as soon as Japan is wrapped up." (“그러니까 속도를 내란 말이야! 필리핀도 브로커든 누구든 연락해서 당장 미팅 잡아. 일본 마무리되는 대로 바로 마닐라로 날아갈 수 있게 세팅하라고.”)

Jeff borrowed the exact tone Patrick had used on him an hour ago and shouted with all his might. (제프는 한 시간 전 패트릭이 자신에게 쓴 그 톤을 그대로 빌려 힘껏 고함쳤다.)

Evan was silent. (에반은 침묵했다.)

Jeff pressed his advantage and poured out the same insults he'd heard from Patrick. (제프는 기세를 몰아 패트릭에게 들었던 모욕을 그대로 쏟아부었다.)

"Evan, you're the man selling a system worth hundreds of millions of dollars. Who would trust weapons sold by someone groaning in a hospital gown? Get your head straight." (“에반, 자네는 수억 달러짜리 시스템을 파는 사람이야. 환자복 입고 골골대는 놈이 파는 무기를 누가 신뢰하겠나? 정신 똑바로 차려.”)

"I clearly understand the directives." (“지시 사항은 명확히 알겠습니다.”)

Evan cut Jeff off. (에반이 제프의 말을 잘랐다.)

"I'll report on the progress in Japan and the Philippines. That's all." (“일본과 필리핀 진행 사항은 보고하겠습니다. 그럼 이만.”)

"What? Hey, Evan—" (“뭐? 이봐, 에반——")

The call ended. (통화가 끊겼다.)

Evan set the phone on the nightstand. Not a single fingertip trembled. The sight of him picking up a glass of water with bandaged hands was so calm you'd never believe he'd just endured his superior's tirade. (에반은 폰을 협탁 위에 올려놓았다. 손끝 하나 떨리지 않았다. 붕대 감긴 손으로 물컵을 집어 드는 옆모습은, 방금 전까지 상사의 폭언을 들은 사람이라곤 믿기지 않을 만큼 평온했다.)

Watching him, Irina put down the apple she'd been peeling and let out a small chuckle. (지켜보던 이리나가 깎고 있던 사과를 내려놓으며 피식 웃었다.)

"Quite composed, aren't you. Is it okay to hang up like that?" (“꽤 의젓하네. 그렇게 해도 되는 거야?”)

Evan took a sip of water and smiled at Irina. (에반은 물을 한 모금 마시고, 이리나에게 미소를 지었다.)

"Probably not, right? But there's no logical point in getting angry at a barking dog." (“안 되겠지? 근데 짖는 개한테 논리적으로 화낼 필요는 없잖아.”)

Evan figured this wasn't the time to fight minnows. The real enemy was across the Pacific. (에반은 피라미와 싸울 때가 아니라고 생각했다. 진짜 적은 태평양 너머에 있으니까.)

item.title: "Democratization is an Independence Struggle"… The Resolution YS and DJ Proclaimed Simultaneously in August 1983 (“민주화는 독립 투쟁이다”… 1983년 8월 YS와 DJ가 동시에 외친 결의)
item.description:
"Democratization is an Independence Struggle"… The Resolution YS and DJ Proclaimed Simultaneously in August 1983 (“민주화는 독립 투쟁이다”… 1983년 8월 YS와 DJ가 동시에 외친 결의)

On August 13, 1983, YS wrote in his diary: "At 8:30 in the morning, I held a historic press conference at home. At the same time, Kim Dae-jung held a joint press conference in Washington." (YS는 1983년 8월 13일 일기에 적었습니다. “아침 8시 30분에 역사적인 기자회견을 집에서 했다. 같은 시간 워싱턴에서 김대중씨가 공동 기자회견을 했다.”)

Ahead of the August 15 Liberation Day, YS and DJ issued simultaneous statements in Seoul and Washington, D.C. The title was "The Struggle for Democratization Is a Struggle for the Nation's Independence and Liberation." They appealed to the people to stand firmly against the dictatorial regime together. YS later revealed in his memoirs that he personally wrote the statement. That day, YS also gave an interview to a Time magazine reporter. (8·15 광복절을 앞두고 YS와 DJ는 서울과 미국 워싱턴에서 동시에 성명을 발표했습니다. ‘민주화 투쟁은 민족의 독립과 해방을 위한 투쟁이다’라는 제목입니다. 국민과 함께 독재 권력에 결연히 맞서야 한다고 호소했습니다. 성명 문안은 YS가 직접 썼다고 훗날 회고록에서 밝혔습니다. YS는 이날 타임지(誌) 기자와 인터뷰도 진행합니다.)

YS continued to carry out activities for democracy. He also met with U.S. Congressman Stephen Solarz, chairman of the House Subcommittee on Asian and Pacific Affairs, who had come to Seoul. (YS는 민주주의를 위한 활동을 지속적으로 전개합니다. 서울에 온 미 하원 아태지구 소위원회 위원장 스티븐 솔라즈 의원과도 만났습니다.)

"I met Chairman Solarz for an hour and ten minutes. We discussed many important things. He said he had visited Gwangju and Busan. He is the first U.S. congressman to do so." (“솔라즈 위원을 1시간 10분 동안 만났다. 여러 가지로 중요한 이야기를 했다. 광주와 부산을 다녀왔다고 한다. 미국 국회의원으로서는 처음이다.”)

Earlier, on August 2, The New York Times had run an article on page two reporting on YS's 23-day hunger strike. It noted that although South Korea was undergoing economic development, it remained under the oppression of authoritarian rule, and that YS, an opposition leader who had escaped house arrest through his hunger strike, was demanding a constitutional amendment for direct presidential elections. (뉴욕타임스는 앞서 8월 2일 자 2면에 YS의 23일간 단식 투쟁을 알리는 기사를 실었습니다. 한국이 경제 발전 중이지만 권위주의 통치의 억압에 놓여 있다, 단식 투쟁으로 가택연금에서 벗어난 야권 지도자 YS는 대통령 직선제 개헌을 요구하고 있다는 내용입니다.)

That summer, temperatures soared to as high as 38 degrees Celsius. YS's struggle for democratization was also heating up. (그해 여름은 최고 섭씨 38도에 이르는 더위가 지속되었습니다. YS의 민주화 투쟁도 뜨거워지고 있었습니다.)

()

Today is an extremely hot day. (오늘은 몹시 무더운 날씨다.)

In this world, there are people who live "for money, or for honor, or for a cause." (이 세상(世上)에는 “돈 때문에 혹(惑)은 명예 때문에 또한 뜻 때문에” 세상(世上)을 사는 사람들이 있다.)

At noon, Publisher Song Seok-ho treated me to a meal. (낮에는 송석호(宋錫昊) 사장(社長)이 사식(私食)을 대접해주었다.)

In the evening, Assemblyman Hwang Myeong-su took me to the Onyang lakeside, where I enjoyed delicious eel with his wife, Comrade Ha, and others. For the first time since the hunger strike, I practiced calligraphy. (저녁에는 황명수(黃明秀) 의원(議員)이 온양 호수가에 가서 장어를 맛있게 부인(婦人)과 하(河)동지(同志) 등(等)과 같이 먹었다. 단식후(斷食後)에 처음으로 서도(書道)를 했다.)

Today is the hottest day of all. The temperature surpassed 38 degrees. (오늘이 최고(最高)로 더운 날이다. 38˚가 넘었으니 말이다.)

Last night, Chairman Jeong Byeong-hun (of Han囗 Condo) came down from Seoul, and in the morning he joined us in our room, chatting pleasantly over breakfast. For lunch, he treated us to rice and chicken stew he had made himself, which we enjoyed at the bungalow. At Chairman Jeong's invitation, I have agreed to go up to Seoul next Sunday. He is truly a kind person. (서울에서 어제 밤에 정병훈(鄭秉勳) 회장(会長)(韓囗콘도)이 내려와서 아침을 우리 방에서 함께 즐겁게 여러가지로 이야기하며 먹었다. 점심은 또한 자기(自己)가 직접 만든 밥과 닭도리탕으로 반가로(*방갈로)에서 맛있게 먹었다. 정(鄭)회장(会長)의 초청으로 내주(來週) 일요일(日曜日) 날에 상경(上京)하기로 했다. 정말 고마운 분이다.)

I visited the birthplace of Chusa. It was my second visit, but it always moves my heart. It is an unbearably hot day. (추사(秋史) 생가(生家)에 다녀왔다. 두 번째 가 보지마는 언제나 마음에 던(*든)다. 너무나도 더운 날이다.)

Another sweltering day above 38 degrees. An astonishing heat wave, the worst in 39 years. (오늘도 38˚가 넘는 무더위다. 39년째의 놀라운 더위다.)

Today, apart from going outside for an hour of morning exercise, I stayed in the hotel all day long. (오늘은 아침 운동을 위해서 한 시간(時間)동안 밖에 나갔을 뿐 하로(*루) 왼종일 Hotel 안에 있었다.)

A phone call came from Im Jeong-gyu in New York. He said that the August 2 issue of The New York Times had prominently featured an article about my press conference on page two. I can't wait to see it. (New york에서 임정규(林井圭)로부터 전화가 왔다. 8월(月) 2일(日)자 New York Times에 2면(面)에 크게 나의 회견(會見) 기사(記事)가 보도(報道)되었다고 하는 전화였다. 빨리 보구 싶구나.)

Today, I practiced calligraphy for the second time (since the hunger strike). I wrote pieces for Chairman Jeong Byeong-hun and Publisher Song Seok-ho. (오늘은 이틀째로 (단식(斷食) 후에 두번째) 서도(書道)를 했다. 정병훈(鄭秉勳) 회장(會長)과 송석호(宋錫昊) 사장(社長) 등(等)에게 글을 써 주었다.)

Hyeon-cheol went up to Seoul ahead of me regarding his matter of going to the United States. (현철(賢哲)이가 미국(美囗) 가는 문제(問題) 때문에 서울에 먼저 갔다.)

Thanks to Chairman Jeong Byeong-hun's kindness, I have decided to go to Seoul on Sunday. (정병훈(鄭秉勳) 회장(会長)의 호의(好意)로 주일(主日)날에 서울로 가기로 했다.)

Yesterday, Hyeon-cheol went to Seoul first, leaving Hye-suk alone. She said she had a good time with her friend yesterday. It had been a while since I had Korean food. (어제 현철(賢哲)이가 먼저 서울에 가고 혜숙(惠淑)이 혼자 남았다. 어제는 혜숙(惠淑)이 친구하고 재미있게 지냈다고 한다. 오랜만에 한식(韓食)을 먹어봤다.)

In the afternoon, I practiced calligraphy. I delivered the pieces to Chairman Jeong Byeong-hun and Publisher Song Seok-ho. They were overjoyed. (오후(午后)에는 서도(書道)를 했다. 정병훈(鄭秉勳) 회장(会長)과 송석호(宋錫昊) 사장(社長)에게 글을 전(傳)했다. 몹시 기쁘(*뻐)한다.)

Secretary Choi came by, and I listened to various stories from him. (최(崔) 비서(秘書)가 와서 여러가지로 이야기를 들었다.)

From Seoul, Comrade Kim Tae-ryong and the secretaries of Assemblymen Ha Je-hong and Hwang Myeong-su came to visit. (서울에서 김태룡(金泰龍) 동지(同志), 그리고 하제홍(河済泓), 황명수(黃明秀) 의원(議員)의 비서(秘書)가 다녀갔다.)

Today, I visited the tomb of Admiral Yi Sun-sin. On the way back, I stopped by Neulbom, a place run by one of our comrades, and had naengmyeon with Comrade Ha Je-hong. It was truly delicious. (오늘은 충무공(忠武公) 묘소에 가봤다. 그길로 늘봄이란 우리 동지(同志)가 하는 늘봄에 가서 하제홍(河済泓) 동지(同志)와 함께 냉면을 먹었다. 정말 맛있다.)

Today, I wrote more calligraphy than ever before—fourteen pieces. I wrote them with the names of our comrades in Onyang. (오늘은 붓글씨를 제일(第一) 많이 썼다. 14장을 써서(*썼으)니 말이다. 온양(溫陽)의 동지(同志)들의 이름을 넣어 썼다.)

While having dinner, I ran into Kwon Oh-hyeon, the publisher of the Busan Ilbo and a fellow alumnus of mine. (저녁을 먹다가 권오(權五)현 부산일보(釜山日報) 사장(社長) 나의 동창(同窓)을 맞(*만)났다.)

Today is Sunday. (오늘은 주일(主日)이다.)

I attended worship service at the Dogo Hot Springs Church. Pastor Kim Deok-hwa presides there. He introduced me publicly. It was bolder than Chunghyeon Church. (도고온천(道高溫泉) 교회(敎會)에서 예배를 봤다. 김덕화 목사(牧師)가 시무한다. 나를 공개적(公開的)으로 소개(紹介)를 한다. 충현교회(敎會)보다 대담하다.)

Amid a send-off from Publisher Song Seok-ho and all the executives, I departed Dogo. Even though it was only a week, I feel a sense of emptiness now that I have left the Dogo Hotel life behind. (송석호(宋錫昊) 사장(社長) 이하 간부(幹部) 전원(全員)이 전송하는 가운데 도고(道高)를 떠나왔다. 도고(道高)Hotel 생활(生活)에서 벗으(*어)나니까 일주일간(一週日間)이지 마는 허전하다.)

No sooner had I arrived in Seoul than this government startled the people again. It issued an air-raid warning—not a security alert. A Chinese MiG-21 had defected. I can only sigh at how much they will make of this and use it for propaganda. (서울데 도착하자마자 이 정부(政府)에서 또 국민(囗民)을 놀라게 한다. 공습 공(*경)보를 발(發)한 것이다. 경비 공보가 아니라 말이다. 중공(中共)의 미그21기(機)가 귀순해 온 것이다. 또 이것을 가지고 얼마나 떠들고 선전을 하겠는지 정말 답답하다.)

Today is another quite hot day. (오늘도 상당(相當)히 무더운 날이다.)

Vice President Lee Min-woo and many others came to visit. (이민우(李敏雨) 부총재(副總裁)와 그 외(外)에 많은 분들이 다녀갔다.)

From Japan, Chairman Kim Seok-won came with a Japanese man. (일본(日本)에서 김석원(金錫沅) 사장(社長)과 일본인(日本人) 한 사람이 같이 왔다.)

Word came from U.S. Congressman Solarz, suggesting we meet at the Chosun Hotel tomorrow at 4:30. (미국(美囗)의 Solarz 의원(議員)이 내일(來日) 4시(時)30분(分)에 조선Hotel에서 맞(*만)나자고 연락이 왔다.)

Many people came by in the morning. (아침에 많은 분들 다녀갔다.)

At noon, since we had gone to Dogo and back, Mi-ae and I went to "Marado" and truly enjoyed a delicious Japanese meal. (낮에는 우리들이 도고(道高)에 갔다 오고 해서 미애와 “마라도”에 가서 정말 맛있게 화식(和食)을 먹었다.)

From Los Angeles, Chairman Cha Sang-Lull, the brother of Director Cha of the bureau, came by and left. (미국(美囗) Los에서 차(車)국장(局長) 동생인 차상(車相)Lull 사장(社長)이 왔다가 갔다.)

At 4:30 in the afternoon, I met for an hour and ten minutes with Congressman Solarz, chairman of the U.S. House Subcommittee on Asian and Pacific Affairs. We discussed many important matters. He said he had visited Gwangju and Busan. He is the first U.S. congressman to do so. (오후(午后)에 4시(時)30분(分) 미국(美囗) 하원(下院)의 아태평양(亞太平洋) 지구(地區) 소위원회(小委員會) 위원장(委員長)인 Solarz 의원(議員)을 1시간(時間)10분(分)동안 맞(*만)났다. 여러가지로 중요(重要)한 이야기를 했다. 광주(光州)와 부산(釜山)을 다녀왔다고 한다. 미국(美囗) 국회의원(國會議員)으로써(*서)는 처음이다.)

I also had a message delivered to Reverend Mun Ik-hwan. (문익환(文益煥) 목사(牧師)님에게도 전(傳)달을 했다.)

From New York, Mr. Kim brought a copy of The New York Times from August 2 containing the article on my press conference. It takes up the entire second page. (New York에서 Mr Kim New York Times의 8월(月)2일(日)자(字)의 나의 회견기사(會見記事)가 있는 신문(新聞)을 가지고 왔다. 2면(面)에 전면(全面)이다.)

At noon, I had lunch with Mr. Kim Byeong-tae and Attorney Oh. (낮에는 김병태(金炳泰)씨(氏)와 오(吳)변호사와 같이 점심을 먹었다.)

Afterward, it was said that a police officer asked to see Mr. Kim Byeong-tae's ID. What an absurd thing. (그 후(后)에 김병태(金炳泰)씨(氏)의 신분증(证)을 보자고 경찰관(警察官)이 봤다고 한다. 정말 어처구니 없는 일이다.)

After a long time, Assemblymen Hwang Nak-ju and Kim Dong-yeong came by, and we talked and discussed plans to attend the unveiling ceremony of Inchon's statue in Gochang on the 15th. (오랜만에 황낙주(黃珞周), 김동영(金東英) 의원(議員) 등(等)이 와서 이야기를 나누며 15일(日)에 고(高)창에 인촌(仁村)의 동상 제막식(式)에 갈 상의(相議)를 했다.)

At noon, I had lunch with Vice President Park Yeong-rok and discussed future matters. (낮에는 박영록(朴永錄) 부총재(副總裁)와 점심을 먹으며 앞으로 문제(問題)를 의논했다.)

In the afternoon, Assemblyman Han Yeong-su came and stayed for a long conversation. (오후(午后)에 한영수(韓英洙) 의원(議員)이 와서 장시간(長時間) 이야기를 하고 갔다.)

Today, I stayed home all day. In the evening, the weather turned very bad, with thunder and heavy rain pouring down. (오늘은 하로(*루) 종일 집에 있었다. 날씨 저녁 때에 몹시 나빠지며 뇌성과 비가 몹시 나(*내)렸다.)

This morning, the weather is very clear. At 8:30 in the morning, I held a historic press conference at home. At the same hour, Kim Dae-jung held a joint press conference in Washington. Im Jeong-gyu and Dr. Jo Hong-gyu called from the United States. That was 6:30 p.m. on the 12th by U.S. time—that is, 8:30 a.m. on the 13th by Korean time. I don't know about other places yet, but the Japanese newspapers are running it as the top story on the front page. (오늘 아침에는 몹시 맑은 날씨다. 아침 8시(時)30분(分)에 역사적(歷史的)인 기자회견(記者會見)을 집에 했다. 같은 시간(時間)인 와신톤(*워싱턴)에 김대중(金大中)씨(氏)가 공동(共同) 기자회견(記者會見)을 했다. 미국(美囗)에서 임정규(林井圭)와 조(趙)홍규 박사(博士)가 전화를 해왔다. 김대중(金大中)씨(氏)가 미국(美囗) 시간(時間)으로 12일(日) 저녁 6시(時)30분(分) 다시 말하면 한국시간(韓囗時間)으로 13일 아침 8시(時) 30분(分)이다. 딴데는 아직 모르겠고 일본신문(日本新聞)들은 일면(一面) 톱이라고 한다.)

In the afternoon, I met with Time magazine correspondent Mr. Chang. (오후에 Time 잡지 기자(記者) Mr 장과 회견(會見)을 했다.)

item.title: Jung and Kim 1%p Apart... Outcome Hinges on Honam and Capital Region Where 70% of Party Members Reside (鄭·金 1%p차… ‘권리당원 70%’ 호남·수도권에 달려)
item.description:
Jung and Kim 1%p Apart... Outcome Hinges on Honam and Capital Region Where 70% of Party Members Reside (鄭·金 1%p차… ‘권리당원 70%’ 호남·수도권에 달려)

As the Democratic Party of Korea's Aug. 17 national convention regional primaries begin with party leader candidates Chung Cheong-rae and Kim Min-seok locked in a 1 percentage point (p) race, the party is set to hold successive primaries in Jeju and Incheon (Aug. 8), followed by Gangwon and Daegu-Gyeongbuk (Aug. 9). The contest is expected to be decided in the Honam region (Aug. 15) and Seoul-Gyeonggi (Aug. 16), where 70% of party members are concentrated. With razor-thin results emerging early in the race, the mudslinging between rival candidates seeking to check each other is also intensifying. <<> On Aug. 3, the party leader candidates' camps offered contrasting interpretations of the voting results from the Chungcheong region and Busan-Ulsan-Gyeongnam party member votes held Aug. 1-2. In the Aug. 1 Chungcheong party member vote, candidate Kim edged out candidate Chung by 303 votes, while in the Aug. 2 Busan-Ulsan-Gyeongnam vote, candidate Chung led candidate Kim by 1,514 votes. Combined, Chung currently holds a 1 percentage point (1,211 votes) advantage. <<> Candidate Kim's camp maintains that winning in unfavorable regions confirms a rising trajectory. The Chungcheong region is home to Chung's hometown (Geumsan, South Chungcheong Province), and Busan-Ulsan-Gyeongnam has many pro-Roh and pro-Moon party members favorable to Chung. On X, Kim wrote, "Having initially projected a 7 percentage point deficit, coming out at minus 1 percentage point in Chungcheong and Busan-Ulsan-Gyeongnam, where I expected stable victories in the end, means my chances of winning have improved significantly." <<> A figure from candidate Chung's camp said, "Chung's momentum was not fully reflected in the Chungcheong region," adding, "The trend of superiority in Busan-Ulsan-Gyeongnam will carry over to other regions as well." On Facebook that day, Chung wrote, "Just as Roh Moo-hyun beat Lee In-je, Chung Cheong-rae will beat Kim Min-seok." This referenced how former President Roh Moo-hyun, who had just over 2% support early in the 2002 presidential primary, overtook candidate Lee In-je in the latter stages. <<> Candidate Song Young-gil, who came in third (9.97%), is pinning hopes on Honam party sentiment. Song is the only one of the three candidates from the Honam region (Goheung, South Jeolla Province). In the Democratic Party leadership election, after regional party member votes are completed, national opinion poll results are combined and announced on the day of the national convention. The party leader and Supreme Council member elections are finalized by combining 70% from delegates and party members' votes with 30% from opinion polls. <<> Inside the party, with the early race so tight, observers expect candidates to focus heavily on Honam and the capital region, where party members are concentrated. South Jeolla-Gwangju and North Jeolla account for 32.9% of all party members, while Seoul-Gyeonggi holds 38.3%. A party official said, "With the one-person-one-vote system for delegates and party members being implemented for the first time, regions with high party member ratios wield absolute influence," adding, "In particular, the results of the Aug. 15 Honam vote, held a day before Seoul-Gyeonggi, are expected to be the inflection point of the contest." <<> As the razor-thin contest continues, the level of mudslinging between the top two candidates is escalating. At a party members' talk concert held in Gangneung, Gangwon Province, that day, candidate Chung Cheong-rae targeted Kim Min-seok's history of leaving the party, saying, "Someone who has betrayed once will betray again. Betrayal has no limits." He added, "Someone who ran away from home for 18 years comes back and demands the deed to the house. Can you trust that?" <<> Meanwhile, at a venue in Jeonju, North Jeolla Province, candidate Kim criticized Chung, the immediate former party leader, saying, "During the first year of President Lee Jae-myung's term, at the most critical time, there was a conflict in the ruling party called the 'Myeong-Jeong clash.'" Kim said, "If the conflict continues, the president will be shaken, mega projects will be shaken, and the fate of this nation could be shaken." He stressed that party-government cooperation is essential for the success of large-scale projects, such as the establishment of a semiconductor plant in Gwangju, South Jeolla Province. <<> In the ruling camp, expectations are that the remaining convention period will be marked by landmines such as the 'Shincheonji interference in the convention' allegations Kim has raised against Chung. After Kim said he would file a complaint with the party's ethics committee against Chung's camp, stating they "engaged in wrongful accusations and incitement," Chung responded that day, saying, "If I become party leader, my first act will be to exercise my authority as party leader to order an ethics investigation into candidate Kim, who endangered the party by raising the Shincheonji allegations." A party official said, "Because this convention holds the power of nomination for the next general election, both sides are fighting with their political lives on the line." (더불어민주당 8·17 전당대회 순회 경선 초반 정청래·김민석 당대표 후보가 1%포인트(p) 차 접전을 벌이는 가운데, 민주당은 제주·인천(8일), 강원·대구·경북(9일)에서 차례로 경선을 치를 예정이다. 승부는 당원의 70%가 몰린 호남(15일)과 서울·경기(16일)에서 판가름날 전망이다. 선거 초반 초박빙 결과가 나오자 상대를 견제하는 후보 간 비방전도 거칠어지고 있다.)

item.title: Yoo Seung-min meets Oh Se-hoon: "We must achieve a grand conservative unity that embraces even those who opposed impeachment" (오세훈 만난 유승민 “탄핵 반대파까지 포용하는 보수 대통합 이뤄야”)
item.description:
Yoo Seung-min meets Oh Se-hoon: "We must achieve a grand conservative unity that embraces even those who opposed impeachment" (오세훈 만난 유승민 “탄핵 반대파까지 포용하는 보수 대통합 이뤄야”)

Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon and former People Power Party lawmaker Yoo Seung-min held a dinner meeting on the 3rd at the official residence of the Seoul mayor in Yongsan-gu, Seoul. It was their first meeting since the June 3 local elections. The two reportedly reached a consensus that the People Power Party must expand its reach through conservative unity. (오세훈 서울시장과 유승민 국민의힘 전 의원이 3일 서울 용산구 서울시장 공관에서 만찬 회동을 했다. 두 사람이 만난 것은 6·3 지방선거 이후 처음이다. 두 사람은 보수 통합을 통해 국민의힘의 외연을 확장해야 한다는 데 공감대를 이룬 것으로 전해졌다.)

The dinner was reportedly arranged to congratulate Mayor Oh on his victory in the Seoul mayoral election and as a gesture of thanks for Yoo's campaign support. On May 21, the first day of official campaigning for the local elections, Yoo accompanied Oh at his rally in the Gangbuk area to support his campaign. At the dinner, Yoo reportedly greeted Oh by saying, "You've been through a lot. How much mental anguish have you endured?" to which Oh responded, "Thank you for making time. My mind has been a bit busy lately." (이날 만찬은 오 시장의 서울시장 당선을 축하하고, 유 전 의원이 선거 유세를 지원한 데 대한 답례 차원에서 마련된 것으로 알려졌다. 유 전 의원은 지방선거 공식 선거운동 첫날인 지난 5월 21일 오 시장의 강북 유세에 동행하며 선거 운동을 지원했다. 유 전 의원은 이날 “고생이 많다. 얼마나 마음고생이 많았느냐”고 인사를 건넸고, 오 시장은 “시간 내주셔서 감사하다. (요즘) 마음이 좀 바쁘다”고 답했다.)

During the subsequent closed-door meeting, Yoo reportedly emphasized the need for a grand conservative unity, saying, "Without embracing even those who opposed the impeachment of former President Yoon Suk-yeol, victory in the general election is impossible." Regarding Oh having kept his distance from party leader Jang Dong-hyuk during the local elections, Yoo reportedly said, "Many people agree that we cannot fight the general election under the current leadership structure, but we must not single out and exclude anyone. If we fight among ourselves, we can never win the general election." Yoo was also reported to have said, "Let's not all get swept up in the atmosphere of dividing people into pro-impeachment versus anti-impeachment, or pro-Yoon versus anti-Yoon." (이어진 비공개 회동에서 유 전 의원은 “윤석열 전 대통령의 탄핵에 반대했던 이들까지 모두 포용하지 않고선 총선 승리가 불가능하다”며 보수 대통합 필요성에 대해 강조한 것으로 전해졌다. 유 전 의원은 오 시장이 지난 지방선거 당시 장동혁 대표와 거리를 뒀던 것과 관련해 “현 지도부 체제로 총선을 치를 수 없다는 점에는 많은 이들이 공감하지만, 누구를 콕 찍어서 배제해선 안 된다”며 “우리끼리 싸우면 절대 총선에서 이길 수 없다”고 말했다고 한다. 유 전 의원은 그러면서 “탄핵 찬성이냐 반대냐, 친윤이냐 비윤이냐 갈라치기 하는 분위기에 우리 모두 휩쓸리지 말자”고 한 것으로 전해졌다.)

Yoo reportedly reiterated the need for conservative unity, stating, "As past experience shows, reform-minded conservatives forming a new party is a path that rarely succeeds." The two had previously bolted from the Saenuri Party (the predecessor of the People Power Party) together during the 2017 impeachment of former President Park Geun-hye and worked together in the Bareun Party. In response, Oh reportedly expressed agreement, saying, "Now is the time to unite the party to the fullest extent. I, too, will play my role in conservative unity." Oh's side said he "expressed deep concern over the reality that the party has not sufficiently sustained its momentum for renewal since the local elections, and that the party's approval ratings have recently declined again." (유 전 의원은 “과거 경험에서 보듯, 개혁 보수가 신당을 차리는 방식은 성공하기 어렵다”며 보수 통합을 재차 강조한 것으로 전해졌다. 두 사람은 2017년 박근혜 전 대통령 탄핵 정국에서 새누리당(국민의힘 전신)을 탈당해 바른정당에서 함께 활동했다. 이에 대해 오 시장도 “지금은 최대한으로 당을 통합해야 한다, (보수 통합에) 저도 역할을 하겠다”며 공감을 표한 것으로 알려졌다. 오 시장 측은 “지방선거 이후 당이 쇄신의 동력을 충분히 이어가지 못한 채 최근 당 지지율마저 다시 하락하는 현실에 대해 깊은 우려를 표했다”고 했다.)

Mayor Oh recently received a first-instance sentence of a 10 million won fine, a ruling that strips him of his mayoral position, on charges of commissioning a poll from political broker Myung Tae-kyun and having a businessman cover the costs. Regarding this, Yoo reportedly said, "You must prepare thoroughly on legal grounds and do everything in your power to secure an acquittal in the second trial." (오 시장은 최근 ‘정치 브로커’ 명태균씨에게 여론조사를 의뢰하고 기업인에게 비용을 대납하게 한 혐의로 1심에서 시장직 상실형인 벌금 1000만원을 선고받았다. 유 전 의원은 이와 관련해 “법리적으로 철저히 대비해 2심에서 무죄를 받아내는 데 사력을 다해야 한다”고 말한 것으로 전해졌다.)

In political circles, there are observations that the two, both considered reform-minded within the party, may cooperate in the process of conservative realignment. Yoo is reportedly meeting with figures both inside and outside the party to build consensus for conservative unity. Oh, for his part, has been meeting in succession with floor leader Chung Point-sik and senior lawmakers including Kim Gi-hyeon and Yoon Sang-hyun since the local elections. (정치권에선 당내 개혁 성향으로 꼽히는 두 사람이 보수 재편 과정에서 공조할 가능성이 있다는 관측이 나온다. 유 전 의원은 최근 당내외 인사들을 두루 만나며 보수 통합을 위한 공감대를 형성하고 있는 것으로 알려졌다. 오 시장 역시 지방선거 이후 정점식 원내대표와 김기현·윤상현 의원 등 중진 의원들을 잇달아 만나고 있다.)

item.title: Former NSC Chief of Staff in Trump's First Term: "Concerns over Coupang and Others Will Persist Until Investment in the US" (트럼프 1기 NSC 비서실장 “대미 투자 전까지는 쿠팡 등 우려 계속”)
item.description:
Former NSC Chief of Staff in Trump's First Term: "Concerns over Coupang and Others Will Persist Until Investment in the US" (트럼프 1기 NSC 비서실장 “대미 투자 전까지는 쿠팡 등 우려 계속”)

Alexander Gray, former chief of staff of the White House National Security Council (NSC), who also served as deputy assistant to the president in the first Trump administration, predicted that "until South Korea delivers on its investment commitments to the US and there is confidence that it is making tangible contributions to American jobs and the manufacturing ecosystem, economic concerns (such as the Coupang issue) will continue to underpin the bilateral relationship." In a recent interview with this newspaper on the 3rd, Gray, who visited South Korea, cited the swift implementation of the $350 billion investment in the US agreed at last year's South Korea-US summit as the most urgent task between the two countries, and made these remarks. <<> Gray, who also served as special assistant to the White House National Economic Council (NEC) for defense industrial base issues during the first Trump administration, said, "President Trump views security and the economy as one," adding, "South Korea's implementation of the investment agreement will be a positive signal for the overall South Korea-US relationship." Gray referenced the Coupang situation and the revised Information and Communications Network Act, noting, "Numerous trends have been detected in which the South Korean government seeks to pursue legislation that discriminates against or disadvantages American companies." On why the White House and Congress are paying attention to such legislative and regulatory measures, he said, "It's not just because of Coupang alone, but rather because of a broad climate and perception that American tech companies are being discriminated against overall." <<> On the possibility of US-North Korea dialogue, Gray said, "In the remaining two years of his term after the November midterm elections, President Trump will seek opportunities to continue his efforts to conclude peace agreements around the world," adding, "It wouldn't surprise me if he tries to negotiate with North Korea again within the next two years." Noting that North Korea's troop dispatch to Russia means, unlike during his first term, the North Korea issue can no longer be separated from Russia and China, he still said, "What only President Trump and the US can do is draw North Korea into negotiations by offering the opportunity for high-level talks with the US." <<> Regarding the delay in South Korea-US consultations on securing South Korea's uranium enrichment rights, he said, "There was an aspect where the relevant personnel within the US government were focused on negotiations with Saudi Arabia," adding, "Once the Middle East crisis subsides, they can refocus on South Korea." On ways for South Korea to make tangible contributions to stability in the Strait of Hormuz, he stated, "In Washington, given the excellent capabilities of the South Korean Navy, there is an expectation that at least one or more warships will be deployed." (트럼프 1기 행정부에서 대통령 부보좌관을 겸임했던 알렉산더 그레이 전 백악관 국가안보회의(NSC) 비서실장이 “한국이 대미 투자 약속을 이행해 미국 내 일자리와 제조업 생태계에 실질적 기여를 하고 있다는 확신이 서기 전까지는, (쿠팡 문제 등) 경제적 우려 사항이 계속 양국 관계의 바탕에 깔려 있을 것”이라고 전망했다. 최근 방한한 그레이 전 비서실장은 3일 본지 인터뷰에서 지난해 한미 정상회담에서 합의한 3500억달러 대미 투자의 신속한 이행을 양국 간 가장 시급한 과제로 꼽으며 이같이 말했다.)

item.title: Rival Factions Clash Within People Power Party Ethics Committee… Chair and Vice Chair Each Demand the Other Step Down (국힘 윤리위 내홍… 위원장·부위원장 서로 “물러나라”)
item.description:
Rival Factions Clash Within People Power Party Ethics Committee… Chair and Vice Chair Each Demand the Other Step Down (국힘 윤리위 내홍… 위원장·부위원장 서로 “물러나라”)

The chair and vice chair of the People Power Party's ethics committee are embroiled in a public feud, each demanding the other step down. The discord reportedly stems from disagreements over the appointment of committee members and meeting procedures, prompting even party leadership to say, "We don't know why they're fighting." The PPP ethics committee had previously faced criticism for "abusing disciplinary action" after courts blocked its attempts to punish members of the pro-Yoon faction. (국민의힘 윤리위원회 위원장과 부위원장이 공개적으로 서로에게 “물러나라”고 요구하면서 내홍을 겪고 있다. 윤리위원 임명과 회의 과정에서 이견이 있었던 것으로 알려진 가운데 당 지도부에서도 “싸우는 이유를 모르겠다”는 이야기가 나왔다. 국민의힘 윤리위는 친한계 인사들을 징계했다가 법원에서 제동이 걸리며 “징계를 남용한다”는 비판을 받았었다.)

Woo Jong-hwan (attorney), vice chair of the PPP ethics committee, and Hwang Kyung-sung (special visiting professor at International Cyber University), a committee member, issued a statement on the 3rd saying, "It would be the proper course of action for Chair Yoon Min-woo (professor at Gachon University) to take responsibility and step down, as a matter of duty to the Jang Dong-hyuk leadership and party members." They claimed that Chair Yoon had shared lists of disciplinary targets with outsiders and urged him to "resign voluntarily before becoming a disciplinary target." Under PPP party rules, the ethics committee must adhere to a "confidentiality obligation." (우종환(변호사) 국민의힘 윤리위 부위원장과 황경성(국제사이버대 특임교수) 윤리위원은 3일 성명을 내고 “윤민우(가천대 교수) 윤리위원장이 책임지고 물러나는 것이 장동혁 지도부와 당원에 대한 도리”라고 했다. 이들은 윤 위원장이 징계 대상자 명단 등을 외부인과 공유한 정황이 있다고 주장하며 “윤리위원장은 징계 대상에 오르기 전에 스스로 퇴진”하라고 했다. 국민의힘 당규에 따르면 윤리위는 ‘비밀 유지 의무’를 준수해야 한다.)

Chair Yoon had previously warned Vice Chair Woo of possible removal. On the 30th of last month, Yoon stated, "If there is a recurrence of violations of the confidentiality obligation regarding internal committee discussions, I will take strict measures, including requesting the party leader to dismiss the committee member in question." This was interpreted as a direct response to Woo's public criticism of the committee's operations. (윤 위원장은 앞서 우 부위원장에 대해 해임 가능성을 경고했다. 윤 위원장은 지난달 30일 “윤리위 내부의 논의와 관련된 비밀 유지 의무 위반이 재발할 경우, 해당 윤리위원의 해임을 당대표에게 요청하는 등 엄정하게 조치하겠다”고 했다. 우 부위원장이 윤리위 운영에 대해 공개적으로 문제를 제기하자 이를 겨냥한 발언으로 해석됐다.)

The ethics committee members, including the chair, were appointed by PPP leader Jang Dong-hyuk. A party leadership official remarked, "We can't understand what purpose they're fighting for." One ethics committee member said, "It reads as nothing more than a power struggle to gain control of the committee, including the chair position," adding, "They could just state their positions during meetings." (위원장을 포함한 국민의힘 윤리위원들은 장동혁 국민의힘 대표가 임명한 사람들이다. 당 지도부 관계자는 “도대체 무슨 목적으로 이들이 싸우는지 이해할 수 없다”고 했다. 한 윤리위원은 “위원장 자리 등 윤리위 주도권을 갖겠다는 다툼으로밖에 읽히지 않는다”면서 “회의에서 입장을 내면 될 일”이라고 했다.)

According to sources familiar with the situation, the conflict escalated after some committee members, dissatisfied with the chair's handling of meetings, resigned and new members were appointed to meet the quorum for voting. Vice Chair Woo said in a phone call with this newspaper, "The problem started with the unilateral appointment of some committee members without consultation." It has been reported that Chair Yoon and some members aligned with him have left the committee's group chat. (윤리위 상황을 아는 관계자 등에 따르면, 이들의 갈등은 위원장의 회의 진행에 불만을 가진 일부 윤리위원이 사퇴하고 의결 정족수를 맞추기 위해 새 윤리위원을 선임하면서 불거졌다고 한다. 우 부위원장은 본지 통화에서 “상의 없이 일부 윤리위원을 일방적으로 임명한 것부터가 문제”라고 했다. 현재 윤 위원장과 그를 따르는 일부 위원이 윤리위 단체 대화방에서 퇴장한 것으로 전해졌다.)

Meanwhile, according to a poll conducted by polling firm Realmeter on the 30th and 31st of last month and released that day, the PPP's approval rating fell 2.9 percentage points from the previous week to 37.7%, while the Democratic Party rose 3.8 percentage points to 45.1%. President Lee Jae-myung's job approval rating hit its lowest level since taking office at 45.9%. (한편 여론조사 업체 리얼미터가 지난달 30~31일 시행해 이날 발표한 정당 지지율 조사 결과에 따르면 국민의힘은 전주 대비 2.9%포인트(p) 하락한 37.7%, 민주당은 3.8%p 오른 45.1%를 기록했다. 이재명 대통령 국정 수행 지지율은 취임 이후 최저치인 45.9%를 기록했다.)

item.title: Military Creates Three New Organizations Including Defense Counterintelligence Headquarters to Replace Disbanded Defense Counterintelligence Command (해체된 방첩사 대신 국방방첩본부 등 軍 3개 조직 창설)
item.description:
Military Creates Three New Organizations Including Defense Counterintelligence Headquarters to Replace Disbanded Defense Counterintelligence Command (해체된 방첩사 대신 국방방첩본부 등 軍 3개 조직 창설)

The Defense Counterintelligence Headquarters, the Defense Security Support Group, and the Security Investigation Division under the Ministry of National Defense Investigation Headquarters have officially launched, taking over the functions of the Defense Counterintelligence Command (hereinafter referred to as the Counterintelligence Command), which was disbanded in the aftermath of the December 3 martial law declaration. The Ministry of National Defense, upon disbanding the Counterintelligence Command, separated counterintelligence information and military internal security duties, establishing the "Defense Counterintelligence Headquarters" and the "Defense Security Support Group" under its direct authority. The security investigation functions were transferred to a separate "Security Investigation Division" created within the Ministry of National Defense Investigation Headquarters. (12·3 비상계엄 여파로 해체된 국군방첩사령부(이하 방첩사)의 기능을 이어받은 국방방첩본부와 국방보안지원단, 국방부조사본부 내 안보수사단이 공식 출범했다. 국방부는 방첩사를 해체하며 방첩 정보와 군 내 보안 업무를 분리해 국방부 산하에 ‘국방방첩본부’와 ‘국방보안지원단’을 신설했다. 안보 수사 기능은 국방부조사본부 내에 별도의 ‘안보수사단’을 만들어 이관했다.)

Minister of National Defense Ahn Kyu-baek attended the inauguration ceremony of the Defense Counterintelligence Headquarters held on the morning of the 3rd at the former Counterintelligence Command building in Gwacheon, Gyeonggi Province, and stated, "What we are parting ways with today is the entire dark history of the counterintelligence agency that served as a 'tool of power' from the May 16 military coup to the December 12 coup, the May 17 martial law, and the December 3 insurrection." Minister Ahn said, "The establishment of the Defense Counterintelligence Headquarters is a major watershed that ends the painful history stained by being a tool of power and completes the rebuilding of a 'military of the people,'" adding, "You must prove for yourselves that you are a 'counterintelligence agency of the people' that the public can trust and rely on." (안규백 국방부 장관은 3일 오전 경기도 과천의 옛 방첩사 건물에서 열린 국방방첩본부 창설식에 참석해 “오늘 우리가 결별하는 것은 5·16 군사정변부터 12·12 쿠데타, 5·17 계엄, 12·3 내란까지 ‘권력의 도구’가 됐던 방첩기관의 어두운 과거 전체”라고 말했다. 안 장관은 “국방방첩본부의 창설은 권력의 도구로 얼룩졌던 지난한 역사를 끝내고 ‘국민의 군대’ 재건을 완성하는 일대의 분수령”이라며 “여러분은 국민이 믿고 의지할 수 있는 ‘국민의 방첩기관’임을 스스로 증명해 내야 한다”고 말했다.)

Major General Pyeon Mu-sam, the former commander of the Counterintelligence Command, has been appointed as acting chief of the Defense Counterintelligence Headquarters. Major General Pyeon, who came from the officer candidate school track, is expected to be officially appointed as the chief of the Defense Counterintelligence Headquarters shortly. He was appointed as acting commander and acting chief of staff of the Counterintelligence Command as a brigadier general in August last year, following the inauguration of the Lee Jae-myung administration, and was promoted to major general in January of this year. (국방방첩본부장 직무대리는 직전 방첩사령관이었던 편무삼 소장이 맡았다. 학사장교 출신인 편 소장은 조만간 국방방첩본부장으로 정식 임명될 예정이다. 그는 이재명 정부 출범 후인 지난해 8월 준장으로서 방첩사령관 직무대리 겸 참모장 대리에 임명됐고, 올 1월 소장으로 진급했다.)

The Ministry of National Defense announced that the newly established Defense Counterintelligence Headquarters will strengthen its counterintelligence response capabilities against North Korea and foreign entities, and focus on blocking leaks of military secrets in the defense industry sector and countering security threats in the cyber domain. The Defense Counterintelligence Headquarters also plans to develop new areas of work, such as counterintelligence support for MRO (maintenance, repair, and overhaul) of U.S. Navy vessels and major strategic assets. (국방부는 신설된 국방방첩본부가 북한과 외국에 대한 방첩 대응 역량을 강화하고, 방산 분야의 군사 기밀 유출 차단과 사이버 영역의 안보 위협 차단에 주력할 방침이라고 밝혔다. 국방방첩본부는 또 미 해군 함정의 MRO(유지·보수·정비)나 주요 전략 자산에 대한 방첩 지원 등 새로운 업무 영역도 발굴할 예정이다.)

The Defense Security Support Group, which will handle military internal security duties, was established at an annex building of the Ministry of National Defense in Yongsan, Seoul. The Defense Security Support Group will be exclusively responsible for central security audits of units at the corps level and above, as well as investigations of security incidents, and will be responsible for preventing military security incidents and protecting military secrets. The Counterintelligence Command's security investigation functions have been inherited by the newly established Security Investigation Division under the Ministry of National Defense Investigation Headquarters, which will exclusively investigate crimes such as espionage, acts of sedition, and leaks of military secrets. <<>> (군 내 보안 업무를 맡을 국방보안지원단은 서울 용산의 국방부 별관에서 창설됐다. 국방보안지원단은 군단급 이상 부대의 중앙보안 감사와 보안 사고 조사 등을 전담하고, 군 보안 사고 예방과 군사기밀 보호 등을 책임질 예정이다. 방첩사의 안보 수사 기능은 국방부조사본부 내에 신설된 안보수사단이 물려받아 간첩, 이적 행위와 군사기밀 유출 등의 범죄를 전담 수사한다.)
